title: dumpcap: Don't write fake IDBs for pcapng interfaces
description:
When we have multiple capture sources, for each one that is a pcapng
source and supplies its own IDBs, don't create a fake IDB with invalid
linktype WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN and write it to the output file.

Instead, use the IDBs from the source, remapping them as necessary.
For non-pcapng sources, store the output IDB interface ID and write
EPBs using that, since now the input interface ID and the output
interface ID are not necessarily the same, if some of the other
sources are not pcapng.

Update the capture tests that use multiple FIFO sources, because now we
don't add two extra IDBs, one for each FIFO. Instead there are
3 * 11 == 33 total IDBs.

This prevents some various incompatibilites in Wireshark and other
tools when a file has interfaces of more than one link type, and also
has IDBs with an illegal WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN link type.

Fix #19080

notes.body:
> Instead, use the IDBs from the source, remapping them as necessary. For non-pcapng sources, store the output IDB interface ID and write EPBs using that, since now the input interface ID and the output interface ID are not necessarily the same, if some of the other sources are not pcapng.

If there is more than one interface, the input interface ID and the output interface ID are not necessarily the same, *even if all interfaces are pipes to which pcapng files are being written*, as each of those files will have an interface numbered 0 if the file has any packets, and, if both of those IDBs are written to the output file, they can't both have an interface ID of 0.

So presumably, unless there's only one input and it's a pipe to which a pcapng file is being written, renumbering of interface IDs is done, as necessary, for all input pcapng files.  (And as for pcap files, at least when writing a pcapng file, an input pcap file can be treated as an input pcapng file with only one section and only one IDB, generated from the pcap file header's link-layer header type and snapshot length, and with no name or description.)

> So presumably, unless there's only one input and it's a pipe to which a pcapng file is being written, renumbering of interface IDs is done, as necessary, for all input pcapng files.

Yes, that's correct, and that's already done. The current dumpcap behavior, before this change:

1. If there is only one input, and it's a pipe to which a pcapng is written, pass through all the blocks directly and don't rewrite anything.
2. If there are multiple inputs, initially create an IDB for all of them, including pipes to which a pcapng is written. For all other inputs, determine the linktype - for a non-pipe, read through libpcap; for a pipe to which a pcap is written, read the header. For a pcapng source, leave it as WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN. These initial IDBs are created in order and will have output IDB interface IDs the same as the input interface number.
3. For non-pcapng sources, when reading packet blocks, write them to the output in EPBs using an output interface ID that matches the input interface ID, since they're the same, because of 2.
4. For pcapng sources, gather all input IDBs and write them to the output, creating a map between the interface ID number in the input and in the output. For any EPBs and ISBs, rewrite the interface IDs according to the map for that source.

This change makes it so that initial IDBs are only created for non-pcapng sources, but no longer created for pipes to which pcapngs are written, that will supply their own IDBs. That means that step 3 has to change for non-pcapng sources, because the EPBs for the non-pcapng sources have to use their output IDB interface ID, which is no longer the same as the input interface number.

Rewriting the outputs interface IDs for pcapng sources was already happening before this patch; the only change is not writing a dumpcap-created IDB with an illegal WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN linktype that no packet was being written claiming to be from that interface.

> For a pcapng source, leave it as WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN.

Or, rather, leave it as "-1", which ends up as 65535 in the pcapng IDB (the link-layer type is a 16-bit unsigned value), which is currently unassigned (and thus the pcapng reader code in libwiretap maps it to `WTAP_ENCAP_UNKNOWN`), but which may be used for specialized purposes in the future (as it's unlikely to be assigned any time soon - if a link-layer header type were to be every 4 days on average, which is a lot more often than it's happening now, that'd last a bit over 700 years - and it's also an "end of range" value that would make it more obvious as meaning something special).

The sooner that all code that calls `capture_loop_init_pcapng_output()` with -1 as the `link_type` argument disappears, the better.

> This change makes it so that initial IDBs are only created for non-pcapng sources

...which, for dumpcap, means "pcap sources", where the one and only link-layer type is in the file header and is thus available before any packets at all are seen.
